raw_response:
My farm is only 4.1 mu, so I have to think carefully how to split it. I will put about 1.5 mu to cotton because cotton price is decent and my family has grown it for years — we know how to manage it. The other 2.6 mu I keep for wheat-maize rotation like most people around here in Quzhou. This way I get grain for the family and cash from cotton.

For wheat this winter, I plan to use improved variety — Jimai or Shi-series, whatever the dealer has that my neighbors used well last year. I will put about two bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15, 50 kg each) as base plus one bag of urea at jointing. That gives me around 16 kg N per mu. I irrigate 3 times: winter water, spring jointing, and grain filling. Sprayed two times for aphids and powdery mildew usually enough.

For summer maize after wheat, I use Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid — everyone buys hybrid now, the old seed gives too little. I put compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress urea when it is knee-high, total about 18 kg N per mu. Rainy season helps, so I only irrigate once if dry. One or two sprays for borer and armyworm.

Cotton needs more work. I buy Bt hybrid seed, costs more but saves pesticide for bollworm. Still I spray 5-6 times for aphids, mites, and lygus. I put more potassium on cotton — it helps boll development. Plough the cotton field deep before planting, rotary for wheat after maize straw.

I want decent yield but I will not waste money. A bit extra fertilizer is fine, but I won't double it.
